name: Nancy Hasley
current_role: Director, Accelerant Holdings (NYSE: ARX); retired as Group General Counsel on March 31, 2026
profile: US-trained insurance/corporate lawyer who was a partner at Sidley Austin (2002-2018) and practised at Keystone Law in London before becoming Group General Counsel of specialty-insurance platform Accelerant from its earliest days in 2019 through its 2025 NYSE IPO. A board member since Oct 2021, her wealth stems from her ARX shareholding.
interesting_fact: She was part of Accelerant from its founding year (2019) through its IPO; the company runs the 'Accelerant Risk Exchange', a data-driven platform matching specialty-insurance underwriters with risk capital. She handed the GC role to Cliff Jenks (ex-RGA) in March 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Accelerant she left a 16-year Sidley Austin partnership to practise at Keystone Law in London (2018-2019), a dispersed-model firm, which is where she was when she joined Accelerant's founding team.

public_contacts.value: Chelsea Allison, COMMAND for Accelerant - chelsea@heycommand.com

notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Confirm she remains on the board post-2026 AGM via the latest ARX proxy. Best route is via Accelerant corporate channels. Insurance-tech angle, not energy.

name: Shaun White
current_role: Founder/CEO, The Snow League; founder, WHITESPACE (snowboard/apparel brand)
profile: San Diego-born snowboarder and skateboarder, a three-time Olympic halfpipe gold medalist (2006, 2010, 2018) and winner of 10 ESPYs, who retired after the 2022 Games. Wealth came from prize money, sponsorships, video games and brand deals. He now runs WHITESPACE (launched 2022) and The Snow League, a pro halfpipe league backed by Ares, Will Ventures and David Blitzer that debuted in 2025.
interesting_fact: The Snow League raised $4.5M seed and a further $30M by Nov 2025; after a first season in Aspen, China and LAAX, its second season opens at Park City Mountain (Jan 21-23), with broadcasts reaching ~175 countries via NBC/Peacock and YouTube.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first guitar as first prize in a snowboarding competition; he later played guitar in the electronic-rock band Bad Things, which took a Saturday headline slot at Lollapalooza 2013 as a last-minute replacement for Death Grips. Tony Hawk befriended and mentored him at age 9 at the Encinitas YMCA skate park.
notes: Celebrity athlete-turned-founder; outreach best via Snow League press channels. Fits entrepreneurship angle (league building, sports-media business). Social handles are his verified accounts; check snowleague.com for a press contact.

name: Brian J. Cali
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Fidelity D & D Bancorp / The Fidelity Deposit and Discount Bank (Dunmore, PA); founder, Cali Law
profile: Northeastern Pennsylvania attorney practising since 1978 and founder of Cali Law (Brian J. Cali & Associates) in Dunmore, focused on family, real-estate, estate and business law. A Fidelity D&D director since 2001 and its chairman, his wealth reflects his long-held FDBC stake and regional business ownership.
interesting_fact: He chaired the Disciplinary Board of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania in 2018 and 2019 - the 13-member independent agency overseeing attorney ethics statewide.
deep_cut_fact: Arts supporter: Super Lawyers lists him as Co-President of the Scranton Cultural Center / Broadway Theatre League; he is also a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers.
notes: Community-bank chairman and local lawyer; no IR email published (bank releases list phone contacts only). Best route is via his law firm or the bank's IR site. Not an energy/data-center figure.

name: Tunç Doluca
current_role: Independent Director, Western Digital (since Aug 2018); director, Analog Devices; retired President & CEO of Maxim Integrated
profile: Ankara-born analog chip engineer who joined Maxim Integrated in 1984 as its youngest design engineer, became VP of R&D in 1993 and in 2007 its second-ever CEO, running the company until its 2021 acquisition by Analog Devices. He designed 40+ products and holds 11 mixed-signal patents; he now sits on the Western Digital and ADI boards.
interesting_fact: As CEO he moved Maxim to a 'hybrid' manufacturing model (own fabs plus foundries) and aligned product development to end markets, before steering the ~$21B all-stock merger into Analog Devices in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: A middle-school model-train set sparked his interest in electronics; a winter-break road trip west with his father led him to UCSB for his MS (1981) - and his father had lived in army barracks on what is now the UCSB campus in 1953. He and wife Lale endowed the Doluca Family Chair in analog/mixed-signal ECE at UCSB.
notes: Low-profile retired semiconductor CEO; no personal accounts found. Strong data-center/storage angle (WDC board). Best route via Western Digital corporate secretary/IR or UCSB College of Engineering, where he is a trustee. Web search budget ran out before an IR email could be confirmed.

name: Michael F. Roman
current_role: Director, Abbott Laboratories (since 2021) and Waystar Holding Corp.; retired 3M Chairman & CEO (retired from 3M May 2025)
profile: Wisconsin-raised electrical engineer who joined 3M in 1988 as a senior design engineer and rose through roles in Europe and Asia (head of 3M Korea, chief strategy officer, Industrial group head, COO) to CEO in 2018 and chairman in 2019. He led 3M through the pandemic N95 surge and the Solventum spin, then stepped down as executive chairman in March 2025.
interesting_fact: During COVID-19 he led 3M's ramp-up of N95 respirator production and publicly pushed back in 2020 on the White House over mask export curbs; he received the Eisenhower Award from Business Executives for National Security in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Stevens Point, Wisconsin, the oldest of five, he played on the UW-Stevens Point Pointers football team (1978-80) before finishing an EE degree at Minnesota, then started his career at Hughes Aircraft and earned a USC master's in electrical engineering before joining 3M.
notes: Now a board-level figure rather than operator; no personal social/press channel found. Best route via Waystar or Abbott corporate secretary. Industrial/manufacturing angle. Web search budget ran out before IR emails could be confirmed.

name: E. Philip Wenger
current_role: Director, Fulton Financial Corp. (Lancaster, PA); former Chairman & CEO (2013-2022)
profile: Career Fulton banker who joined the Lancaster, PA bank in 1979 and worked through retail, commercial, operations and systems roles, chairing Fulton Bank (2006-09), serving as Fulton Financial's President (2008-17) and COO, then Chairman and CEO from 2013 through 2022. He remains on the board; his wealth reflects decades of FULT stock.
interesting_fact: He spent his entire 40+ year career at one institution, rising from an entry role in 1979 to lead a ~$25B-plus-asset regional bank holding company for a decade.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Advisory Board of the Stonier Graduate School of Banking and sat on the board of Operation HOPE Global, the financial-dignity nonprofit; he is also a past chair of the Lancaster Chamber of Commerce.
notes: Don't confuse with Philip R. Wenger (Isaac's restaurants founder / Lancaster Conservancy), a different Lancaster civic leader. Low public profile; route via Fulton corporate secretary. Web search budget ran out before IR/press email could be confirmed.

name: Ryan Petersen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Flexport (San Francisco); venture partner, Founders Fund
profile: Bethesda-raised Berkeley economics grad who ran an import-export business in China, co-founded trade-data firm ImportGenius (2007), then founded tech-driven freight forwarder Flexport in 2013 (Y Combinator 2014). Flexport hit an $8B valuation in 2022; Petersen handed the CEO role to Amazon's Dave Clark, then returned as CEO in Sept 2023 and bought Convoy's assets.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2021 his Twitter thread proposing fixes for the LA/Long Beach port backlog (e.g. relaxing container-stacking limits) went viral and reached Gov. Gavin Newsom; local authorities adopted some of his suggestions.
deep_cut_fact: At 17 he and his brother David started an import-export business buying goods from China and selling them on eBay; he moved to China in 2005 to run it, before an MBA at Columbia (2008).
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly; active on X (@typesfast) and does many podcasts/TV hits on tariffs, Hormuz and supply-chain risk. Good energy/logistics angle. No published press email found on Flexport's newsroom.

name: John C. (Jack) Roche
current_role: President & CEO, The Hanover Insurance Group (Worcester, MA) since Oct 2017; Richard Lavey is named CEO-elect (succession under way)
profile: Property-casualty insurance veteran of 40+ years who started in underwriting at Atlantic Mutual and Fireman's Fund, held senior roles at St. Paul Travelers, then joined The Hanover in 2006, running business insurance and Hanover Agency Markets before becoming CEO in 2017. His wealth reflects THG equity awards; the company has named a CEO-elect to succeed him.
interesting_fact: He has led The Hanover, one of the oldest US P&C insurers (founded 1852) that sells exclusively through independent agents, for nearly a decade.
deep_cut_fact: A UConn BA graduate, he sits on the board of overseers of St. John's University's Maurice R. Greenberg School of Risk Management, Insurance and Actuarial Science, and on the boards of The Institutes and the American Property Casualty Insurance Association.
notes: Goes by 'Jack'. Leadership page lists Richard W. Lavey as CEO-elect, so Roche may be stepping down soon - time-sensitive. Route via Hanover media relations. Insurance (incl. climate/catastrophe risk) angle rather than energy.

name: Brady M. Murphy
current_role: President & CEO and Director, TETRA Technologies (NYSE: TTI), The Woodlands, TX (CEO since 2019)
profile: Penn State chemical engineer and Harvard AMP alum with 35+ years in energy: 26 years at Halliburton (incl. SVP Global Business Development & Marketing), then CEO of upstream-tech firm Paradigm Group, before joining TETRA as COO and becoming CEO in 2019. He is repositioning TETRA from oilfield fluids toward bromine, energy-storage electrolytes and water/power solutions.
interesting_fact: TETRA's new Arkansas bromine plant is on schedule and within 12 months of mechanical completion (Q3 2026), electrolytes for energy storage are driving chemicals growth, and four of seven TETRA Oasis pipeline projects are tied to data centers or their power needs.
deep_cut_fact: Before his 26-year Halliburton career he started out at Gerhart Industries, and at Halliburton ran the Europe/Sub-Saharan Africa region; he holds a B.S. in chemical engineering from Penn State.

public_contacts.value: Giselle Piller, Sr. Director Global Marketing & Communications - gpiller@onetetra.com

notes: Excellent podcast fit: energy transition (bromine, zinc-bromide battery electrolytes, produced-water/lithium) plus data-center power via TETRA Oasis. Route via TETRA media relations.

name: Christopher Gavigan
current_role: Founder & CEO, Prima (botanical wellness brand); co-founder, The Honest Company
profile: UCSB environmental-science grad and former science teacher who ran the nonprofit Healthy Child Healthy World and wrote its 2008 book, then co-founded The Honest Company with Jessica Alba and Brian Lee in 2012, serving as Chief Product and Brand Officer through its 2021 IPO. He went on to found and run Prima, a plant-based wellness brand.
interesting_fact: His 2008 book 'Healthy Child Healthy World: Creating a Cleaner, Greener, Safer Home' carried a foreword by Meryl Streep.
deep_cut_fact: Before consumer goods he taught ecology and science in LA and the Bay Area and founded Pinnacle Expeditions, an adventure-travel company for teenagers; UCSB gave him its 2019 Outstanding Alumni Award in Environmental Sciences.
notes: Sustainability/clean-products angle. Web search budget ran out before his verified social accounts or Prima press contact could be confirmed - check Prima's website and his Instagram/LinkedIn. Avoid family references.

name: Walter Driver
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Scopely (Culver City, CA; part of Savvy Games Group)
profile: Co-founded mobile-games developer/publisher Scopely in Los Angeles in 2011 with Ankur Bulsara, Eric Futoran and Eytan Elbaz, and co-leads it as Co-CEO. Scopely built a portfolio of licensed and original free-to-play games, passed $1B lifetime revenue in 2019, and was acquired by Saudi Arabia's Savvy Games Group for $4.9B in 2023; it remains independently run.
interesting_fact: Scopely's Monopoly Go! (April 2023) was the biggest mobile game of 2023 with ~$1B revenue and became the fastest mobile game ever to gross $3B; Scopely ranks as the #2 mobile game developer worldwide and #1 in the US by revenue (2024).
notes: Gaming/consumer-tech founder, less of an energy fit. Web search budget ran out before his personal background or a Scopely press email could be verified; check scopely.com newsroom or LinkedIn.

name: Mikhail Predtechensky
current_role: Co-founder and Scientific Director, OCSiAl (graphene nanotubes; HQ Leudelange, Luxembourg); Full Member, Russian Academy of Sciences
profile: Novosibirsk physicist (b. 1957, Gusinoozyorsk, Buryatia) who led the molecular-structure physics department at the Kutateladze Institute of Thermophysics, then co-founded OCSiAl in 2009-10 on his industrial method for synthesising single-walled carbon nanotubes. OCSiAl became a unicorn in 2019 (Daikin invested at ~$1.7B in 2021) and is the world's largest graphene-nanotube producer, used in lithium-ion battery materials.
interesting_fact: OCSiAl is the only company with EU REACH registration to produce single-walled carbon nanotubes at up to 100 t/year; it opened a 60 t/yr plant in Serbia in Oct 2024 and plans a hub in Differdange, Luxembourg.
deep_cut_fact: Long before nanotubes he worked on energy tech: his research includes an electrochemical fuel cell that directly oxidises solid hydrocarbons such as coal, and an arc plasma generator with molten electrodes. He won the 2019 Russian State Prize in Science and Technology and holds 18 patents/certificates.
notes: Name often transliterated Predtechensky/Predtechenskiy. Scientist-founder, likely more comfortable in Russian. Strong battery-materials/energy angle. Route via OCSiAl press office.

name: Jeff Chapin
current_role: Co-founder and former Chief Product Officer, Casper Sleep (current role not verified)
profile: Princeton civil engineer and Stanford product-design MS who spent a decade as a designer at IDEO (2003-2013) before co-founding mattress brand Casper in 2014 with Philip Krim, Neil Parikh, Luke Sherwin and Gabe Flateman, serving as Chief Product Officer from 2013 through the 2020 IPO. Casper was taken private in 2022 and sold to foam maker Carpenter Co. in 2024.
interesting_fact: He led product at Casper from day one - the company's original one-mattress, bed-in-a-box design - growing it from a $1.85M seed round to a 2020 NYSE listing.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2013, just before Casper, he founded Common Made LLC, a platform for designers to tackle societal issues, which he ran as Principal until 2016; his undergraduate degree is in civil engineering, not design.
notes: Designer-founder; current venture unknown (web search budget exhausted). Check LinkedIn/personal site for current role before outreach. Casper founders list: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper_Sleep
